correctness.rationale: Bézout gives 33=n2+2t+3n3; parity of the 18 conic-line intersection multiplicities forces the single node to lie away from conic-line incidences and yields tCL=9-y-z and tCC=1+y+z. Three lines are either concurrent (one LLL triple) or a triangle (z=2 or 3 occupied vertices). The written proof exhausts concurrent and triangular assignments, applying at most two tangents from an external point, per-side Bézout budgets, and the dual Bézout obstruction preventing a line from being tangent to conics already mutually tangent at two ordinary tacnodes. Every case violates the required tCC. The independent necessary-condition finite overapproximation explored 72 combinatorial cases and found zero feasible; this corroborates, but does not substitute for, the projective proof. Gałecka nearly free identities at m=9 and orbifold bound leave only (1,10,4),(0,9,5), giving the conditional corollary.
residual_risks: The exclusion is for distinct smooth conics and lines over C with only three specified ordinary singularity types.
The remaining basket (0,9,5) is a necessary near-freeness condition; neither realizability nor near freeness follows from these counts.

final_claim: A reduced union of exactly three distinct smooth complex conics and three distinct lines with only A1 nodes, A3 ordinary tacnodes and D4 transverse triple points cannot have (n2,t,n3)=(1,10,4). Consequently a nearly free arrangement of this component type, if it exists, must have basket (0,9,5), not asserted realizable.
